messages.author: fb5d69b072117c9e
messages.subject: ddply and POSIXlt
parts:
Hi all,

Here's an issue I ran into - apparently my data.frame has some
variables of type POSIXlt and it is causing problems with ddply. I'm
not entirely certain what the difference is between POSIXct and
POSIXlt and how my data ended up in the format of the latter, but this
isn't the first time I've had issues with date-time formats and plyr.

Here's my example - notice that the first works and the second
doesn't.

z <- c(1, 2, 3, 3)
x <- seq_len(length(z))
a <- as.POSIXlt(z, origin="1960-01-01")
b <- as.POSIXlt(z, origin="1970-01-01")

# works
df <- data.frame(x, a, b)
ddply(df, .(a, b), function(df) df[1,])

# doesn't work
df <- data.frame(x)
df$a <- a
df$b <- b
ddply(df, .(a, b), function(df) df[1,])

Do I just need to be more careful with date-time formats? Or is this a
bug?

Thank you,

-ricardo

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: ddply and POSIXlt
parts:
It's fixed in the devel version of plyr, and you can work around it by
manually casting dates to as.POSIXct.

Hadley

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ddply and POSIXlt
parts:
Hi:

Here are some differences between POSIXlt and POSIXct objects; it may
explain why certain things that work with POSIXct objects do not
necessarily extend to POSIXlt objects (and vice versa):

> z <- c(1, 2, 3, 3)
> x <- seq_len(length(z))
> a <- as.POSIXlt(z, origin="1960-01-01")
> b <- as.POSIXlt(z, origin="1970-01-01")

> str(b)
POSIXlt[1:4], format: "1969-12-31 16:00:01" "1969-12-31 16:00:02" ...
> d <- as.POSIXct(b)
> str(d)
POSIXct[1:4], format: "1969-12-31 16:00:01" "1969-12-31 16:00:02" ...
> class(b)
[1] "POSIXlt" "POSIXt"
> class(d)
[1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"
> mode(b)
[1] "list"
> mode(d)
[1] "numeric"

# Some components of the POSIXlt list
# If memory serves, there are nine components in all
> b$year
[1] 69 69 69 69
> b$mon # Jan = 0
[1] 11 11 11 11
> b$hour
[1] 16 16 16 16
> b$min
[1] 0 0 0 0
> b$sec
[1] 1 2 3 3
> d$year
Error in d$year : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

because d is a numeric vector, not a list.

Hope this clarifies a few things.
Dennis

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Re: ddply and POSIXlt
parts:
The fundamental problem is that POSIXlt and POSIXct values are not actually "objects" in the object-oriented programming sense -- that is, defined only by the operations that are meaningful on them -- the underlying representation "leaks out".  This is a problem with base (S3) R itself, where method dispatching is often (but not always) supported, but abstraction through information hiding is not.  There are better object systems available, but much of R is S3-based.

               -s
